clauses.scope_note: Section 5.2 prohibits using service-related brand identifiers in any way, alone or in combination, and separately prohibits displaying, using, or seeking registration of related trademarks or domain names, and representing a right to deal with the identifiers.
clauses.condition_explanation: deepseek_permission means permission from DeepSeek. The prohibition applies absent that permission.

obligation_items.content: Do not use, display, or apply to register the specified service-related brand identifiers, or represent a right to display, use, or otherwise deal with them, without DeepSeek's permission.
obligation_items.object: DeepSeek-related trademarks, service marks, trade names, domain names, website names, logos, URLs, and other prominent brand features
obligation_items.trigger: Whenever the licensee or an end user would use, display, register, or represent a right to deal with a specified identifier without DeepSeek's permission.

clauses.scope_note: Section 5.3 lists improper uses of DeepSeek brand identifiers: implying a special relationship beyond technology provider/API user; misleadingly presenting DeepSeek as co-creator, contributor, investor, or endorser; using misleading cooperation or endorsement descriptions; and associating brand elements with the specified unlawful, noncompliant, sensitive, or rights-infringing content or scenarios.
clauses.condition_explanation: The listed acts are prohibited uses of brand identifiers. The list is introduced as non-exhaustive.

obligation_items.content: Do not use DeepSeek brand identifiers to imply a special relationship beyond technology provider and API user; mislead others about co-creation, contribution, investment, or endorsement; describe the relationship using misleading cooperation or endorsement terms; or associate the identifiers with the specified improper content or scenarios.
obligation_items.object: DeepSeek brand identifiers and their presentation or association
obligation_items.trigger: Whenever the licensee uses or associates DeepSeek brand identifiers in a manner described in Section 5.3.

clauses.scope_note: Section 5.4 makes any Section 5 breach fundamental regardless of actual damage and reserves DeepSeek's rights to terminate, forfeit unconsumed account balance, pursue breach liability, and require a public statement confirming no special cooperative relationship.
clauses.condition_explanation: brand_section_breach means a breach of any provision of Section 5. This clause reserves remedies to DeepSeek; it does not itself require the user to make a statement unless DeepSeek requires one.

obligation_items.content: Issue a public statement confirming that no special cooperative relationship exists between the parties if DeepSeek requires it as a remedy for a Section 5 breach.
obligation_items.object: Public statement concerning the parties' relationship
obligation_items.trigger: A Section 5 breach occurs and DeepSeek requires the statement.

clauses.scope_note: Section 5.5 states DeepSeek's Privacy Policy does not cover personal information processing when end users access downstream systems, applications, or functions developed by the licensee based on the open platform; the licensee, as controller in that scenario, should disclose its relevant privacy policy to end users.
clauses.condition_explanation: The disclosure duty applies in the specified downstream end-user access scenario. The excerpt does not specify the contents or timing of the disclosure.

obligation_items.content: Disclose the relevant privacy policy to end users whose personal information the licensee processes as controller through its downstream systems, applications, or functions.
obligation_items.object: Relevant privacy policy for personal information processing in the licensee's downstream systems, applications, or functions
obligation_items.trigger: End users access those downstream systems, applications, or functions and the licensee acts as controller of the personal information processing.

clauses.scope_note: Section 6.1 says prepayment may be required, usage consumes the balance, and DeepSeek reserves suspension or termination if the balance is insufficient. DeepSeek may adjust fees according to business circumstances.
clauses.condition_explanation: paid_service_use means use of a paid service. prepayment_if_required means prepayment only where required; the text does not state that every paid service requires prepayment.

obligation_items.content: Prepay for the Services when prepayment is required and maintain sufficient balance for paid-service usage.
obligation_items.object: Payment balance for the paid Services
obligation_items.trigger: The licensee uses a paid Service for which prepayment is required; usage consumes the balance.

clauses.scope_note: Section 6.2 makes recharge methods, prices, consumption methods, and free quotas subject to product-page and platform information; permits adjustments. For adjustments significantly affecting rights, DeepSeek must promptly notify by a prominent method. Continued use after adjustment signifies acceptance.
clauses.condition_explanation: significantly_affects_rights is the stated threshold for DeepSeek's prompt-notice duty. Continued use after an adjustment is treated as acceptance; the clause does not make continued use mandatory.

obligation_items.content: Promptly notify the user of an adjustment that significantly affects the user's rights, using a prominent method such as an in-site notification, website announcement, or email.
obligation_items.object: Notice of the significant adjustment to price or paid services
obligation_items.trigger: DeepSeek makes an adjustment that significantly affects the user's rights.

clauses.scope_note: Section 6.3 says the user shall carefully confirm the order, account, and information when recharging. The recommendation to buy according to actual dosage is advisory, not a duty.
clauses.condition_explanation: recharging means making a recharge purchase.

obligation_items.content: Carefully confirm the recharge order, account, and information.
obligation_items.trigger: Before or when making a recharge.

clauses.scope_note: Section 6.3 describes contacting DeepSeek through Section 11 or platform customer service, cooperating with relevant proof, and DeepSeek review. If approved, only remaining unspent account amounts are refunded in one lump sum after necessary costs such as handling fees; no partial refund, and spent amounts are not refunded.
clauses.condition_explanation: Refund is not guaranteed: it is subject to approval. The excerpt does not provide Section 11 or specify what proof is required.

obligation_items.content: Provide relevant proof materials and cooperate with review of the refund request.
obligation_items.object: Proof materials relating to the refund request

obligation_items.content: If the refund is approved, refund the remaining unspent account amount in one lump sum after deducting necessary costs; do not refund spent amounts or provide partial refunds.
obligation_items.object: Approved refund of remaining unspent account balance

clauses.scope_note: Section 6.4 promises and guarantees the legality of funds used to recharge. DeepSeek may request documentation to verify fund legality and may take Section 7.2 measures if it believes or determines the obligation was breached.
clauses.condition_explanation: The funds-legality duty applies to funds used for recharging. The verification request and enforcement measures are DeepSeek's reserved rights.

obligation_items.content: Use only funds that are legal for recharging.
obligation_items.object: Funds used to recharge the account

clauses.actor_role: licensee and end users; licensee must procure and guarantee end-user adherence
clauses.scope_note: Section 7.1(a) requires the licensee to procure and guarantee that it and its end users follow the stated principles, obey applicable law, avoid infringing others' legitimate rights or seeking improper gains, and avoid disrupting normal internet-platform order.
clauses.condition_explanation: The licensee's procurement and guarantee duty covers both itself and end users. The listed standards apply to their service use.

obligation_items.content: Procure and guarantee that the licensee and its end users act voluntarily, equally, fairly, and in good faith; comply with applicable law; do not use the service to infringe others' legitimate rights or seek improper gains; and do not disrupt normal internet-platform order.
obligation_items.object: Licensee's and end users' use of the Service
obligation_items.trigger: The licensee or an end user uses the Service.

clauses.scope_note: Section 7.1(b) imposes joint and several liability for losses and damage to DeepSeek arising out of or relating to end users' breach of Section 7.1(a). This is an operative liability allocation, not a use permission or an independently represented activity constraint.
clauses.condition_explanation: The trigger requires an end-user breach of Section 7.1(a) and losses or damage to DeepSeek arising out of or relating to that breach. The available activity/object schema cannot faithfully express the resulting liability allocation or payment obligation.

clauses.scope_note: Section 7.1(c) says, to the extent permitted by applicable law, disputes between the licensee and end users shall be resolved solely between them and DeepSeek shall be released from them. This is a dispute allocation/release, not an activity constraint representable by the available schema.
clauses.condition_explanation: The provision is expressly limited by applicable law. The clause does not create a distinct allowed activity or service-use duty.

clauses.scope_note: Section 7.2 reserves DeepSeek's discretion to take listed enforcement measures, including warnings, correction deadlines, restrictions, suspension, account closure, re-registration prohibition, and content deletion, without prior notice. DeepSeek may announce results and decide whether to restore use. For suspected legal violations or illegal activity, it will retain records, report to competent authorities as required by law, and cooperate with investigations. The licensee is assigned responsibility for resulting third-party claims and must compensate DeepSeek for specified losses and expenses. The discretionary sanctions and compensation allocation are not a faithful permission/prohibition model of the listed activities.
clauses.condition_explanation: The three enforcement triggers are alternatives. The legal reporting and record-retention language applies to suspected legal or illegal conduct. Compensation is tied to third-party liabilities, claims, demands, or losses resulting from the specified conduct and losses incurred by DeepSeek in protecting its rights.

obligation_items.content: Retain relevant records, report suspected law-violating or illegal conduct to competent authorities in accordance with law, and cooperate with their investigations.
obligation_items.object: Records and reports concerning suspected violations or illegal activities
obligation_items.trigger: Behavior is suspected of violating laws or regulations or involves illegal activities.

obligation_items.content: Compensate DeepSeek for losses incurred in protecting its rights, including the enumerated fees, expenses, compensation, liquidated damages, settlement costs, and administrative fines.
obligation_items.trigger: Third-party legal liabilities, claims, demands, or losses result from the conduct described in Section 7.2 and DeepSeek incurs rights-protection losses.

Section 5.5 refers to the DeepSeek Privacy Policy, and Sections 6.3 and 7.2 refer to Sections 11 and 7.2 respectively; the incorporated policy and any additional referenced procedures are not supplied here.

Section 7.1(b), Section 7.1(c), and portions of Section 7.2 create liability, release, discretionary-remedy, or legal-procedure consequences that cannot be faithfully represented as activity permissions/prohibitions with the available schema; these limits are identified rather than treated as general use rules.
Section 6.1 and 6.2 describe user payment and provider fee-setting, not a licensee's right to Charge or SellCopies.

paragraph_audit.reason: Section 5.2 prohibits specified brand-identifier uses absent DeepSeek permission.
Section 5.3 is a heading introducing the specific improper brand-use prohibitions in the following paragraphs; it imposes no separate operative rule.
Section 5.3(1) prohibits implying a special relationship beyond provider/API user.
Section 5.3(2) prohibits misleading brand placement or presentation.
Section 5.3(3) prohibits misleading cooperation or endorsement descriptions.
Section 5.3(4) prohibits the specified improper associations of brand elements.
Section 5.4 states breach consequences and reserves remedies, including a possible required public statement.
Section 5.5 assigns the licensee a downstream privacy-policy disclosure duty in the stated controller scenario.
Section 6.1 addresses possible prepayment, balance consumption, and suspension or termination for insufficient balance.
Section 6.2 specifies paid-service terms, adjustment discretion, notice threshold, and acceptance by continued use.
Section 6.3 includes a recharge-confirmation duty and conditional refund process; its advisory purchasing suggestion is not modeled as a duty.
Section 6.4 requires lawful recharge funds and describes verification and enforcement rights.
Section 7.1 heading and introductory words introduce the following operative subparagraphs; they create no separate activity rule.
Section 7.1(a) imposes the service-use standards and the licensee's duty to procure and guarantee end-user adherence.
Section 7.1(b) is an operative joint-and-several liability allocation for specified losses, not faithfully representable as an activity constraint.
Section 7.1(c) allocates disputes and releases DeepSeek subject to applicable law; the operative release cannot be represented faithfully as an activity rule.
Blank line; no operative text.

Section 7.2 creates discretionary enforcement rights and liability consequences that cannot be fully expressed as activity constraints; the available clause records the triggers and specified obligations but not the full remedy structure.
Section 7.2(a) is an enforcement trigger based on suspected or determined breach; enforcement consequences are discretionary and not fully representable.
Section 7.2(b) is an enforcement trigger based on service disruption or significant threat; enforcement consequences are discretionary and not fully representable.
Section 7.2(c) makes payment breach an enforcement trigger; the full discretionary remedy structure is not representable.

This paragraph includes discretionary restoration and announcement rights, mandatory legal record-retention/reporting/cooperation language, and a compensation allocation; not all operative content is faithfully representable.
Section 7.3 is a limitation-of-liability and damages provision, excluded from this activity-constraint extraction.
Section 7.4 is a warranty disclaimer, excluded from this activity-constraint extraction.
